identification.summary: Russian nation-state actor focused on email credential theft through tailored, rapport-building spear-phishing of individuals in international affairs, defense, logistics support to Ukraine, think tanks, academia, NGOs and government, mainly in NATO countries [S1][S2][S5]. Microsoft says its activity has historically supported both espionage and cyber-influence objectives [S1]. The UK NCSC and allied agencies assess it is almost certainly subordinate to FSB Centre 18 [S5][S6]. Since at least 2022-2023 it has added selective custom malware (SPICA, LOSTKEYS, and the NOROBOT/MAYBEROBOT chain) to its phishing operations [S4][S9][S11].
identification.firstObserved: Microsoft has tracked the actor since 2017 [S2]. NCSC reporting (via coverage) describes activity since at least 2015, including spear-phishing of UK parliamentarians [S6].
identification.notes: Microsoft name: Star Blizzard (formerly SEABORGIUM; renamed April 2023) [S2]. Microsoft says its indicators and tactics overlap with Callisto Group (F-Secure), TA446 (Proofpoint) and COLDRIVER (Google) [S2]. Google lists COLDRIVER as also known as UNC4057, Star Blizzard and Callisto [S4]. The December 2023 joint advisory (per search summary) lists SEABORGIUM, Callisto Group, TA446, COLDRIVER, TAG-53 and BlueCharlie as aliases [S5]. Ukraine's SSU associated Callisto with Gamaredon (ACTINIUM), but Microsoft said it had not observed technical intrusion links supporting that association [S2]. Citizen Lab's COLDWASTREL is assessed as a distinct actor targeting similar communities and must not be merged with Star Blizzard [S10][S12].

attribution.sponsor: Russian Federation, Federal Security Service (FSB). The UK NCSC and partners assess Star Blizzard is almost certainly subordinate to FSB Centre 18 [S5][S6]. DOJ described the group as an operational unit within FSB Center 18 (per coverage of the October 2024 seizure) [S8].
attribution.confidence: Government: NCSC uses 'almost certainly' for Centre 18 subordination (December 2023), jointly with US and other Five Eyes agencies [S5][S6]. Microsoft calls it a Russian nation-state actor without a formal confidence rating [S1]. Google calls COLDRIVER 'Russian government-backed' without naming an agency [S4].
attribution.basis: Joint advisory and NCSC attribution statement [S5][S6]. US charges (December 2023) against Ruslan Peretyatko, described as an FSB Center 18 officer, and Andrey Korinets, with US Treasury and UK sanctions and a State Department reward of up to $10 million (per press coverage) [S7]. Microsoft and Google telemetry and infrastructure analysis [S1][S2][S4]. Microsoft civil action and DOJ domain seizures in October 2024 [S8].

objectives: Intelligence collection in support of Russia's strategic interests, per Google [S4]. Microsoft assesses it likely supports traditional espionage and information operations rather than financial goals [S2]. In a small number of cases stolen material has been leaked, including hack-and-leak operations against UK officials and an NGO, and NCSC links it to leaks intended to interfere in UK politics [S4][S6]. It also targets exiled Russian opposition figures and Western civil society [S10].

sectors: Government and diplomacy, current and former officials [S3][S4]
Defense and intelligence consultancies; defense-industrial firms (from 2022) [S2][S5]
US government agencies including the intelligence community, DoD and defense contractors, State Department and Department of Energy facilities (2016-2022, per indictment coverage) [S7]
Think tanks and Russia-focused international-relations researchers [S2][S3]
NGOs, IGOs and civil society, including funders [S2][S8][S10]
regions: United States and United Kingdom (most targeted) [S2][S5]
Other NATO countries, with occasional Baltic, Nordic and Eastern European targeting [S2][S5]
targeting.notes: The actor mainly targets personal or NGO email accounts rather than corporate ones [S4][S5]. About 30% of Microsoft's nation-state notifications for this actor went to consumer email accounts [S2]. Microsoft observed targeting of more than 30 organizations in 2022 and more than 30 civil-society organizations between January 2023 and August 2024 [S2][S8].

capabilities.summary: Core tradecraft: reconnaissance of targets, fake social-media profiles and new webmail accounts impersonating trusted contacts, then benign rapport-building emails, often referencing a non-existent attachment, before any malicious link [S2][S5]. It harvests credentials with Evilginx adversary-in-the-middle pages, which capture passwords and MFA tokens [S1][S2]. Lures include custom PDFs, password-protected PDFs or Proton Drive links, and altered OneDrive notifications (July-August 2024) [S1]. Evasion includes HubSpot and MailerLite redirect URLs, multiple registrars, link shorteners, open redirects, Microsoft Safe Links abuse, browser fingerprinting, hCaptcha, a DNS/reverse-proxy service and randomized domains [S1]. Microsoft says it adopts TTPs for brief periods and changes them once they are publicly known [S1]. After compromise it exfiltrates mail and sets forwarding rules to dead-drop accounts [S2]. In November 2024 it used QR codes to link targets' WhatsApp accounts to actor-controlled devices, its first use of WhatsApp [S3]. Selective malware: the Rust backdoor SPICA, delivered as a fake PDF decryption tool and believed in use since November 2022 [S9]; LOSTKEYS, a VBS file stealer delivered through a ClickFix fake CAPTCHA and PowerShell chain (January-April 2025) [S4]; and, after LOSTKEYS was exposed, the COLDCOPY lure, NOROBOT DLL, YESROBOT Python backdoor and MAYBEROBOT PowerShell backdoor (May-June 2025) [S11].

campaigns.name: Institute for Statecraft compromise
campaigns.summary: NCSC says the UK think tank was compromised in 2018 and its founder's account from December 2021, with documents leaked in both cases (per search summary of NCSC release).

campaigns.name: UK-US trade documents leak
campaigns.summary: NCSC says the group compromised UK-US trade documents that were leaked ahead of the 2019 UK general election (per search summary).

campaigns.name: Brexit proponents ProtonMail leak
campaigns.summary: Emails allegedly stolen from consumer ProtonMail accounts of Brexit proponents were leaked; Microsoft independently linked the operation to SEABORGIUM.

campaigns.name: Microsoft SEABORGIUM disruption
campaigns.summary: Microsoft disabled actor accounts and published details, citing campaigns against more than 30 organizations since the start of 2022.

campaigns.name: SPICA backdoor deployment
campaigns.summary: Google TAG observed SPICA from September 2023, delivered via fake PDF decryptors, and believes it has been used since November 2022.

campaigns.name: Joint advisory, NCSC attribution, US indictment and sanctions
campaigns.summary: NCSC and partners attribute Star Blizzard to FSB Centre 18; the US charges Peretyatko and Korinets; the US and UK impose sanctions.

campaigns.name: 'Rivers of Phish' civil-society campaign
campaigns.summary: Citizen Lab and Access Now tie spear-phishing of exiled Russian opposition figures, NGO staff, funders and media in the US and Europe to COLDRIVER.

campaigns.name: Microsoft/DOJ domain takedown
campaigns.summary: Microsoft's Digital Crimes Unit obtained an order covering 66 domains and DOJ seized 41 more; Microsoft expected the actor to rebuild infrastructure.

campaigns.name: WhatsApp account-takeover phishing
campaigns.summary: Emails impersonating a US government official offered a WhatsApp group on supporting Ukraine NGOs; a QR code linked victims' accounts to actor devices. Microsoft disclosed it in January 2025.

campaigns.name: LOSTKEYS ClickFix malware
campaigns.summary: GTIG observed LOSTKEYS delivered through a fake CAPTCHA and PowerShell chain in January, March and April 2025, in highly selective cases.

campaigns.name: ROBOT malware chain
campaigns.summary: After LOSTKEYS was exposed, GTIG (per coverage) reports a move to COLDCOPY, NOROBOT and YESROBOT (late May 2025), then MAYBEROBOT (early June 2025).

diamond.adversary: FSB Centre 18-linked operators (NCSC: almost certainly) [S5][S6]. US charges name Ruslan Peretyatko, described as an FSB officer, and Andrey Korinets [S7].
diamond.capability: Evilginx AiTM credential and MFA-token theft; PDF, Proton Drive and OneDrive-themed lures; WhatsApp device linking; SPICA, LOSTKEYS and NOROBOT/YESROBOT/MAYBEROBOT malware [S1][S3][S4][S9][S11].
diamond.infrastructure: Actor-registered domains across multiple registrars, VPS servers running Evilginx, a DNS/reverse-proxy service, email marketing platforms (HubSpot, MailerLite) as redirectors, link shorteners, and newly created webmail sender accounts (often Proton) [S1][S2]. Over 100 domains were seized in October 2024 [S8].
diamond.victim: Government, defense, think-tank, academic, NGO, journalist and politician targets in the US, the UK and NATO, often through personal email; Russian exiles [S2][S4][S5][S10].
diamond.socioPolitical: Collection on Russia, Ukraine and NATO policy; selective leaks intended to interfere in UK politics; targeting of Russian dissidents abroad [S4][S6][S10].
diamond.technology: Consumer and cloud email, phishable MFA, WhatsApp linked-device features, and Windows scripting (PowerShell via the Run dialog, rundll32) [S1][S3][S4][S11].

gaps: Primary government documents were not opened: the joint advisory, NCSC news pages, DOJ press release, indictment and Treasury designation were blocked. Their content comes from search summaries and press coverage [S5][S6][S7][S8].

Original Google TAG SPICA blog, GTIG October 2025 ROBOT-chain report, Citizen Lab 'Rivers of Phish' report and Zscaler's BAITSWITCH/SIMPLEFIX report were not opened; details come from search results and secondary coverage [S9][S10][S11].

Vendor naming: TAG-53 and BlueCharlie (Recorded Future), IRON FRONTIER (Secureworks) and GOSSAMER BEAR (CrowdStrike) come from the imported record or advisory alias lists and were not checked against the vendors' own reporting.
COLDWASTREL (Citizen Lab) and PwC's related tracking are assessed as distinct from COLDRIVER; the relationship is unresolved [S10][S12].
The SSU-proposed link to Gamaredon (ACTINIUM) is unconfirmed by Microsoft [S2].
Google could not confirm whether December 2023 Maltego-themed LOSTKEYS samples belong to COLDRIVER [S4].
The year of the Institute for Statecraft compromise differs across reports (2018 vs 2019) [S6].
No public reporting on activity after October 2025 surfaced in searches; search results showed NCSC PDFs re-hosted under 2026 paths, but their content could not be opened.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Key terrain is the personal email, cloud accounts and messaging apps (WhatsApp) of senior leaders, policy advisers, defense-industrial staff, Ukraine-assistance logistics personnel and their outside contacts. Much of this sits outside DoD network boundaries [S1][S3][S5]. STEP 2: Reliance on credible impersonation and phishable MFA makes identity the operating environment. Rapid TTP and infrastructure turnover after public exposure shortens indicator lifespan [S1][S3][S8]. STEP 3: The template is reconnaissance and a fake persona, a benign rapport email, a PDF, link or QR lure, Evilginx credential and token capture or WhatsApp device linking, then mailbox exfiltration and forwarding rules. A selective malware branch runs from a ClickFix fake CAPTCHA through PowerShell to LOSTKEYS or the NOROBOT/MAYBEROBOT chain [S1][S2][S3][S4][S11]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued credential phishing of personal accounts of US, UK and NATO defense and policy figures for intelligence on Ukraine support and Russia policy. MDCOA is a timed leak of stolen planning or political correspondence during a crisis or election to undermine allied cohesion [S4][S6]. Candidate indicators: unsolicited mail from known contacts on new webmail addresses; mail citing a missing attachment; password-protected PDFs or Proton Drive links; Safe Links-wrapped shortened URLs; new inbox forwarding rules; unexpected WhatsApp linked devices; PowerShell or rundll32 launched from the Run dialog after a CAPTCHA page [S1][S2][S3][S4][S11].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: victims are mostly personal and NGO accounts, so DoD sensors will miss much of this activity. JCC2 pictures should include partner reporting from NCSC, Microsoft and Google [S2][S4][S5]. (2) Authorities: personal accounts and commercial messaging platforms fall outside DODIN defensive authorities. Response there relies on FBI, DOJ and industry actions such as the October 2024 domain seizures [S7][S8]. (3) Mission assurance: phishing-resistant MFA and personal-account hygiene for key leaders and Ukraine-support staff reduce exposure to AiTM credential theft. Script-execution restrictions reduce ClickFix risk [S1][S4]. (4) Coordination: share indicators with Five Eyes partners and the DIB, and expect rapid infrastructure rebuilding after exposure [S5][S8].

provenance.importedSummary: The Callisto Group is an advanced threat actor whose known targets include military personnel, government officials, think tanks, and journalists in Europe and the South Caucasus. Their primary interest appears to be gathering intelligence related to foreign and security policy in the Eastern Europe and South Caucasus regions.
